headline: Granted variances for a 7.67-foot side setback and 37% impervious coverage at 104 Lincoln Street; denied a variance at 86 Dessa Drive without prejudice.
summary: A survey found the addition at 104 Lincoln Street, built for Ms. Amaro's mother, sits within 7.67 feet of the eastern property line. The surveyor also measured impervious coverage at 37%, not the 32% approved earlier. Board members later discussed requiring land surveys with future applications.
decisions: Denied the variance for 86 Dessa Drive without prejudice, 5-0.
Granted variances for a 7.67-foot side yard setback and 37% impervious coverage at 104 Lincoln Street, 5-0.
Approved the October 15, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 4-0 with one abstention.
Approved the 2027 regular meeting schedule as proposed, with all members in favor.

November 24, 2026 
The Hamden Zoning Board of Appeals held a hybrid Public Hearing and Regular Meeting on 
Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7:00pm. The meeting was held in-person in the 3rd Floor Conference 
Room at Hamden Government Center (2750 Dixwell Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518) and remotely via 
Town Zoom teleconferencing software at https://hamden.zoom.us/j/82445626188. 
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Paul Fioretti (Chairman), Nancy Saravis-Foote, John 
Brantley, Steve Walsh, Francesca Provenzano 
  Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Maisie Albis 
(Commission Clerk) 
Via Zoom: Genevieve Bertolini (Stenographer) 
  
Chairman Fioretti called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. Board members and staff introduced 
themselves.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
  Chairman Fioretti called for public comments relating to topics within purview of Board that 
were not already on the agenda; there were none. The Chairman closed the public comment session. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Public Hearing 
 1. Variance #26-6740 
86 Dessa Drive 
Applicant: Lisa Haylon 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
i. requesting 7-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
As the applicant was not present, the Board opted to begin with the public hearing for 
Variance #26-6741 (104 Lincoln Street).  
The clerk addressed the remote attendee to determine if that individual was the applicant 
using a Zoom account under a different name; there was no response. Chairman Fioretti 
recommended tabling the item. He asked the clerk how long the application had been under 
review thus far. She noted that the hearing had opened at the previous meeting, within the
Page 2 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 11.19.26 Minutes 
 
statutory 65-day timeline. However, the previous meeting was exactly 35 days prior; the present 
meeting was the deadline to close the hearing.  
Commissioner Provenzano asked whether the timeline could be extended. Mr. Livshits 
explained that the applicant would have to agree to grant that extension. As she was not present 
and had not communicated such agreement prior to the meeting, Mr. Livshits did not feel that the 
hearing could continue beyond the statutory 35 days. He recommended that the Board deny the 
application without prejudice, which would allow the applicant to resubmit the application if she 
chooses to. Members agreed and Chairman Fioretti closed the hearing.  
 
2. Variance #26-6741 
104 Lincoln Street 
Applicant: Colleen and Ernesto Amaro 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
i. requesting 7.67-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
(2) Section 220 Table 2.1 
ii. requesting 37% impervious coverage where a maximum of 30% is allowed 
Attorney Bernard Pellegrino represented applicants Colleen and Ernesto Amaro, who were 
also in attendance. Mr. Pellegrino stated that the property had come before the Board earlier in 
the year with a similar request as part of the same project; the Board had granted a variance to 
allow 32% impervious coverage where a maximum of 30% is allowed. The approval allowed the 
Amaros to construct an addition so that Ms. Amaro’s mother can move in with the couple, with a 
handicap-accessible bedroom and bathroom on the ground floor to accommodate her mobility 
limitations. 
When attempting to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy, the Amaros were told that the addition 
appeared to be encroaching on the side yard. A land survey revealed that the new construction 
was within 7.67 feet of the eastern property line. Further, the surveyor calculated the impervious 
coverage to be 37% rather than 32% as approved. Mr. Pellegrino explained that the Amaros are 
seeking the two new variances to bring the now-existing addition into compliance so that a CO 
may be issued.  
Chairman Fioretti asked what factor drove the change in the impervious coverage calculation 
result. Mr. Pellegrino replied that the contractor who had been working with the Amaros had 
relied on assessor’s maps and GIS tools for property details, which do not always provide 
accurate lot lines. When the calculation was performed based on the correct parcel size, which 
was smaller, the percentage of impervious coverage was slightly higher.  
Commissioner Saravis-Foote [asked] if a survey had been done prior to the first application 
process. Commissioner Brantley followed up to Mr. Pellegrino’s reply by asking why the builder
Page 3 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 11.19.26 Minutes 
 
had not completed one. Mr. Pellegrino was unsure, and said that he had been unable to speak with 
the builder ahead of the meeting.  
Commissioner Provenzano [asked] if the addition had perhaps been built slightly larger than 
designed or out of its intended place. Mr. Pellegrino denied both and said the mismatch in the as-
designed and as-built conditions resulted from the lot calculation errors.  
Members had no further questions. Chairman Fioretti then opened the floor to comments from 
the public. There were neither comments in favor of nor opposed to the proposal, and the 
Chairman closed the public hearing for the item. 
 
C. Regular Meeting 
 
1. Variance #26-6740 
86 Dessa Drive 
Applicant: Lisa Haylon 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
i. requesting 7-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
Commissioner Provenzano moved to deny the requested variance without prejudice as 
the applicant was not in attendance and had not yet presented her proposal at the 
expiration of the hearing timeline. Commissioner Brantley seconded the motion and all 
members voted in favor. The variance request was denied without prejudice. 
 2. Variance #26-6741 
104 Lincoln Street 
Applicant: Colleen and Ernesto Amaro 
Variance requested from: 
(1) Section 220 Table 2.3 
i. requesting 7.67-foot side yard setback where a minimum of 12 feet is required 
(2) Section 220 Table 2.1 
ii. requesting 37% impervious coverage where a maximum of 30% is allowed 
Chairman Fioretti called for discussion or a motion on the item. He noted that he would view 
the application favorably as presented, independent of the prior application. Commissioner Walsh 
agreed. He said that constructing the required accessible living space would be impossible on the 
undersized lot without a variance. He added that the Amaros had relied on their contractor and 
made their proposal in good faith. For those reasons, Commissioner Walsh moved to grant the 
requested variances to allow a 7.67-foot side yard setback and 37% impervious coverage. 
Commissioner Saravis-Foote seconded the motion.
Page 4 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 11.19.26 Minutes 
 
Commissioner Provenzano stated that she agreed with Commissioner Walsh and the 
Chairman; she would look favorably at the application had it been the initial proposal. She also 
raised concerns. She noted that the Board cannot grant variances due to self-created hardships, 
and that the basis of the current request is something that has already built by the applicant. 
Members discussed her point. Mr. Livshits clarified that the hardship itself—a land-based 
hardship stemming from the undersized lot and the need for handicap accessibility—was 
unchanged from the original application.  
Chairman Fioretti admitted that it may have been an oversight for the Board to not require a 
land survey with the first application. He suggested that surveys be required going forward. Mr. 
Livshits appreciated the suggestion and felt it should be implemented. The Chairman then 
acknowledged that requiring a full survey could add significant costs for the applicant, but that 
the Board should at least require accurate up-to-date lot lines.  
With no further discussion, the Chairman called for a vote on the motion. All members voted 
in favor; the requested variances for a 7.67-foot side yard and 37% impervious coverage 
were granted unanimously. 
 
 D. Old Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of October 15, 2026, Public Hearing and Regular Meeting Minutes 
` Commissioner Brantley moved to approve the minutes as written, seconded by 
Commissioner Provenzano. Chairman Fioretti and Commissioners Brantley, Provenzano, 
and Saravis-Foote voted in favor. Commissioner Walsh had not been present and thus 
abstained. The minutes were approved as written with four in favor and one abstention.   
   
E. New Business 
 
 
 
 
      
 
1. Review Proposed 2027 Regular Meeting Schedule 
 Commissioner Brantley moved to approve the proposed 2027 Regular Meeting schedule. 
Commissioner Saravis-Foote seconded and all were in favor. The 2027 Regular Meeting 
schedule was approved as proposed. 
 2. Discussion: Board Membership 
 Commissioner Brantley asked Mr. Livshits if there were any new prospective members. Mr. 
Livshits said there were none at this time. Commissioner Saravis-Foote recalled that she joined 
the Board after attending a Town Boards and Commissions Fair, and asked if there would be 
similar events in the future. Mr. Livshits said he intends to speak with Town Clerk Karimah 
Mickens regarding possible community engagement events and recruitment for membership. He 
will try to give an update at the next meeting. 
Commissioner Brantley mentioned that he received notice from the Town Clerk’s office that 
his term was expiring. The notice requested that he apply by November 1 if interested in
Page 5 of 5 Zoning Board of Appeals 11.19.26 Minutes 
 
reappointment, but he had not seen it in time. Mr. Livshits assured him that he should still apply 
if he was willing to serve another term. 
Commissioner Provenzano inquired about the current demographics of the Board with respect 
to Legislative Council District and political party. The Hamden Town Charter encourages 
geographic and political diversity by mandating that no more than two members live in the same 
district and requiring minority party representation. Commissioner Provenzano would like to try 
to recruit members and said she will prioritize those who are from other districts and parties. 
 
3. Land Use Commissioner Trainings 
 Commissioner Provenzano asked if there were any upcoming commissioner training sessions. 
Mr. Livshits said that there has been a bit of a lull in opportunities as UCONN CLEAR, which 
provides much of the training, has been seeking a new educator. He advised members that there 
were free pre-recorded training sessions available on the UCONN Land Use Academy website. 
He believed all members were up-to-date with their training at this time. 
 4. Discussion: Requiring Surveys with Applications 
 Chairman Fioretti and Mr. Livshits returned to the question of whether applicants should be 
required to provide surveys, with the Chairman asking under what circumstances Mr. Livshits 
would find one to be absolutely necessary. Mr. Livshits replied that it can be difficult to know 
ahead of time. He added that requiring a survey would likely benefit applicants during their 
permitting process.  
 
F. Adjournment  
 
Commissioner Brantley made a motion to adjourn. Commissioner Saravis-Foote seconded 
and all were in favor. Chairman Fioretti adjourned the meeting at 7:51 p.m.
